{{Current events|year=2019|month=09|day=27|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[American intervention in Libya (2015–present)]]
**The [[United States Africa Command]] says the US has carried out an airstrike against [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant in Libya|ISIL]] in southwest [[Libya]], killing at least 17 militants. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/africa/the-us-says-it-has-carried-out-an-airstrike-against-the-islamic-state-group-in-libya (''The Straits Times'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Collapse of Thomas Cook]]
**[[Portugal]] announces it has set aside 150 million [[euro]]s to lend to the companies that have been hurt by the collapse of tour guide company [[Thomas Cook Group|Thomas Cook]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-portugal-tourism-thomascook/portugal-sets-aside-150-million-euros-to-offer-credit-to-firms-hit-by-thomas-cook-collapse-idUSKBN1WC1DY?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[September 2019 climate strikes]], [[Individual and political action on climate change]]
**An estimated two million people across the world participate in [[September 2019 climate strikes|strikes to encourage action on climate change]], with a total of 6 million during the week, including up to 500,000 protesters in [[Montreal, Quebec]], [[Canada]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2019/sep/27/climate-crisis-6-million-people-join-latest-wave-of-worldwide-protests (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/get-a-unique-view-inside-and-above-montreal-s-half-million-climate-march-1.5301122 (CBC)]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of China]], [[Foreign relations of Taiwan]], [[Foreign relations of Kiribati]], [[Cross-Strait relations]]
**[[Sinophobia|Anti-China]] protests are held by the [[Parliamentary opposition|opposition]] in [[Kiribati]]'s capital of [[Tarawa]] after the government severed ties with [[Taiwan]] and established relations with [[China]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/399747/opposition-organises-anti-china-protest-march-in-kiribati (RNZ)]
*[[Turkey–United States relations]]
**[[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] says that it is "impossible" for his country to stop buying oil from [[Iran]], despite [[United States sanctions against Iran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-iran-trade-usa/erdogan-says-turkey-will-continue-oil-natural-gas-trade-with-iran-ntv-idUSKBN1WB33D (Reuters)]
*[[Seventy-fourth session of the United Nations General Assembly|U.N. General Assembly 74th session]], [[Foreign relations of North Macedonia]]
**[[North Macedonia]] establishes [[Foreign relations of North Macedonia|diplomatic relations]] with [[Armenia]], [[Monaco]], [[San Marino]] and [[Tunisia]] at the [[Seventy-fourth session of the United Nations General Assembly|74th session]] of the [[United Nations General Assembly]]. [http://mfa.gov.mk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=3229:74-5&catid=52:press-releases&lang=en&Itemid=684 (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of North Macedonia)] [https://news.am/eng/news/535883.html (News.am)] [https://twitter.com/Dimitrov_Nikola/status/1177679851697901568 (Foreign Minister of North Macedonia)]
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**Diplomats of several Western-aligned countries walk out of the [[UN]] General Assembly as [[Venezuela]]n Vice-President [[Delcy Rodríguez]] begins a speech.[https://www.foxnews.com/politics/diplomats-walk-out-in-protest-as-venezuela-attempts-to-fill-un-general-assembly-with-supporters (Fox News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Honour killing in Pakistan]]
**The brother of [[Pakistanis|Pakistani]] [[social media]] star [[Qandeel Baloch]] is sentenced to life in prison for her [[honour murder]], while six others are acquitted. The case sparked international headlines and discussion of [[women's rights in Pakistan|women's rights in the country]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-49848384 (BBC)]
*[[Crisis in Venezuela]]
**A resolution is adopted by the [[United Nations Human Rights Council]] with 19 votes in favour, 7 against and 21 abstentions, accusing [[Venezuela]]'s [[Nicolás Maduro]] government of thousands of [[extrajudicial murder]]s, [[forced disappearance]]s, and [[torture]], after being proposed by the [[Lima Group]] and backed by many European countries. The UN resolves to send an investigative mission to the country. Maduro says the motion was "produced by the [[United States]] to run a hate campaign". Another Venezuelan representative calls the [[United Nations|UN]] a "small group" that they "will not cooperate with". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-49855018 (BBC)]
*Police in [[Kaduna]], [[Nigeria]], raid an Islamic learning centre, and free around 500 men and male children held captive there. The freed detainees allege torture, [[slavery in contemporary Africa|slavery]], and sexual abuse, and some display evidence of injury and [[malnutrition]]. Two children self-identify as being from [[Burkina Faso]], with the remaining captives thought by police to be mostly Nigerian. Eight suspects are arrested. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-49850408 (BBC)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] is formally referred to the [[Independent Office for Police Conduct]] (IOPC) amid allegations of corruption during his tenure as [[Mayor of London]]. Johnson is alleged to have awarded a close friend, American technology entrepreneur [[Jennifer Arcuri]], "thousands of pounds" in public business funding, according to the ''[[The Sunday Times]]''. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2019/sep/27/boris-johnson-referred-to-police-watchdog-over-potential-misconduct (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Trump–Ukraine controversy]], [[Impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump]]
**[[Kurt Volker]], United States special envoy to [[Ukraine]], resigns one day after the release of a [[whistleblower]] report  concerning a phone call between U.S. President [[Donald Trump]] and Ukraine President [[Volodymyr Zelensky]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/09/27/politics/kurt-volker-resigns/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-whistleblower-ukraine-volke/trump-envoy-to-ukraine-volker-resigns-sources-idUSKBN1WC2L6 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 United States federal budget]]
**[[President of the United States]] Donald Trump signs a short-term spending bill that temporarily extends government funding through November 21, thereby avoiding a [[Government shutdowns in the United States#Federal government|federal government shutdown]] when the 2019 budget funding ends on September 30. [https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/463464-trump-signs-stopgap-measure-funding-government-through-november (''The Hill'')] [https://www.cnn.com/2019/09/27/politics/trump-signs-short-term-spending-bill/index.html (CNN)]
